baseline_models.focus_anchor: The form-II ك ذ ب verbs at words 2 and 4 repeat across the present conditional and the completed past clause.
baseline_models.mechanism: The conditional present and completed past carry the same act from current addressees to earlier collectivities. The focus therefore transfers a social operation, assigning falsehood to a messenger, across times rather than merely comparing two private beliefs.

activation_trace.role: The literal attribution-of-falsehood branch makes both verbs one repeated social act and links the present protasis to the past apodosis.

changed_reading.before: If the present audience rejects the messenger, earlier peoples also rejected messengers.
changed_reading.after: The present audience is entering a historically recurrent social act: assigning falsehood to the messenger in the same grammatical form used of earlier peoples.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: قَبْلَهُمْ at word 5 places قَوْمُ and the named peoples anterior to the present deniers.
baseline_models.mechanism: Temporal precedence is primary, but the facing branch of ق ب ل makes the earlier peoples stand before the current audience as a confronting precedent. The collective branch of ق و م prevents the comparison from shrinking to isolated individuals: one social body is placed before another.

activation_trace.role: The literal temporal-priority branch supplies the historical ordering on which the precedent mechanism depends.
The facing branch turns what is earlier into something set before the present audience for comparison and confrontation.
The people-as-collective branch makes the compared units social bodies rather than a series of private doubters.

changed_reading.before: The verse supplies old examples that happened earlier.
changed_reading.after: The verse sets an earlier collective directly before the current collective as a precedent they must face, making history an active counterpart to the present conditional.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The proper name عَادٌ at word 8 is inventoried under ع و د, whose proper-name and return branches coexist.
baseline_models.mechanism: The proper-name branch controls the literal reading, while the return-after-departure branch resonates with the repeated ك ذ ب form and قَبْلَهُمْ. The list can consequently carry a latent self-description: the old pattern returns as the verse names 'Ad.

activation_trace.role: The proper-name branch keeps 'Ad as the literal historical people and constrains the wordplay.
The return-after-departure branch gives the proper name a latent recursive role inside the repeated denial pattern.
The repeated attribution branch supplies the event that appears to return from the earlier peoples into the present.

changed_reading.before: 'Ad is one proper name in a list of peoples who denied.
changed_reading.after: Without ceasing to be a proper name, 'Ad becomes a latent hinge announcing that the earlier act of denial is returning in the present.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding sequence joins empowerment to establishing and maintaining communal practice; the focus then names a denying قَوْم. This recasts the denying people as an organized collective that upholds a social order, coexisting with the simpler reading of qawm as a group label.

activation_trace.role: The literal people-group branch anchors the changed reading in the focus noun قَوْمُ.
The care, maintenance, and governance branch makes the adjacent أَقَامُوا an activator for collective order-maintenance in the focus qawm.
The empowerment branch supplies the capacity by which a collective can establish and maintain a public order.

structural_cues: 22:41 immediately precedes the focus and repeats the ق و م root in أَقَامُوا before 22:42 uses قَوْمُ.
The sequence shifts from an empowered plural subject with public practices to named singular grammatical peoples who deny.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies empowerment, establishment, and the repeated ق و م root; I infer that lexical adjacency transfers institutional agency from أَقَامُوا to قَوْمُ. A live alternative is that قَوْمُ remains only an ordinary collective noun with no governance coloring.

changed_reading.before: Earlier groups happened to reject messengers.
changed_reading.after: Earlier qawm, and potentially the current audience, act as organized counter-orders whose denial protects a maintained collective arrangement.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's earlier denials are expanded by two repetitions of extended time followed by taking to account, with an explicit time-count between them. Historical precedent therefore describes a delayed process rather than an immediate reaction: denial, interval, then seizure.

activation_trace.role: Temporal precedence anchors the process in the focus's earlier peoples.
The repeated attribution of falsehood supplies the initiating act whose later course the context unfolds.
The extension-of-time branch supplies a real interval after denial rather than an immediate consequence.
The taking-to-account branch closes the first extended interval with consequential seizure.
The time-counter and recurrence branch makes the intervening scale of a counted day part of the delay mechanism.
The split inventory's respite branch repeats the extension of the interval for another unjust town.
The second taking-to-account branch confirms the repeated interval-to-seizure sequence.

structural_cues: 22:44 orders denial, respite, then seizure; 22:48 repeats respite, then seizure around 22:47's enlarged timescale.
The conjunction ثُمَّ marks sequence with delay in both contextual closures.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two respite-to-seizure sequences and a counted timescale; I infer that they unpack the temporal mechanics latent in قَبْلَهُمْ. The live alternative is that these verses console the messenger without prescribing a uniform schedule for every denial.

changed_reading.before: Earlier denial functions as a generic warning, easily heard as implying prompt punishment.
changed_reading.after: Earlier denial establishes a recurrent but delayed process in which an extended, counted interval can separate public rejection from consequential seizure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The named qawm are followed by gathered settlements rendered empty, collapsed, unused, and partly still raised, then by an instruction to travel and reason. The list of peoples can thus function as an index to materially inspectable traces, not only as a recited genealogy.

activation_trace.role: The people-group branch provides the human collectives whose names can be spatially materialized in settlements.
The facing branch lets anterior peoples become evidence placed before perception rather than remaining remote chronology.
The branch of people gathered in a settlement converts a named qawm into an inhabited spatial form.
The collapse branch supplies the visible failure of the settlement's built form.
The emptiness and disuse branch makes an abandoned resource a surviving negative trace of the people.
The raised and reinforced building branch supplies a durable positive trace alongside collapse and disuse.
The going and movement branch turns the traces into an itinerary available to present observers.
The reason-that-restrains-ignorance branch assigns the traveled material traces an evidentiary function.

structural_cues: 22:45 immediately follows the completed people-list in 22:42-44 and shifts from names to ruined settlement features.
22:46 then asks whether they have traveled in the earth and acquired hearts with which to reason.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the adjacency of named peoples, ruined material features, travel, and reasoning; I infer a referential arrow from the names to a field of readable traces. A live alternative is that 22:45 broadens to other towns rather than identifying remains of the listed peoples one for one.

changed_reading.before: Noah's people, 'Ad, and Thamud are remembered names supporting an argument from report.
changed_reading.after: The names point toward a traversable archive of collapsed structures, unused resources, and surviving monuments through which the present can reason about earlier denial.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus says peoples denied before them, while 22:52 speaks of messengers and prophets before you. These opposed deictic centers create two predecessor lines, denying communities and sent messengers, whose recurrence intersects in the present conditional.

activation_trace.role: Temporal priority locates denying peoples before the current audience.
The same temporal branch locates messengers before the current messenger, creating the second predecessor line.
The messenger-and-message branch identifies the office recurring on the other side of the denier sequence.
The succession branch supplies seriality to the messenger line and makes it structurally comparable to the people-list.

structural_cues: The pronouns cross: 22:42 has before them, whereas 22:52 has before you.
Both constructions place the present encounter inside a past sequence without making either sequence the sole frame.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two ق ب ل constructions with different deictic objects and a messenger succession; I infer that they form paired historical lines meeting in the focus. A live alternative is that the repeated adverb is ordinary chronology without deliberate counterpoint.

changed_reading.before: The focus aligns the present audience only with a lineage of past deniers.
changed_reading.after: The present confrontation is the meeting point of two recurrent lineages: communities before them that deny and messengers before you who are sent.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus conditional can sound episodic, but 22:55 supplies continuing unbelief in doubt until a sudden boundary, and 22:57 repeats the denial root with signs as its object. Denial can therefore be carried as a self-maintaining state whose long duration and abrupt end coexist.

activation_trace.role: The focus attribution branch anchors the state in the act of declaring the messenger false.
The duration branch in the no-longer construction extends rejection from an event into a continuing condition.
The second mapped target independently supplies continuing action, preserving the split inventory inside the duration mechanism.
The doubt-and-hesitation branch supplies the internal medium in which the continuing rejection persists.
The suddenness branch provides an abrupt terminal boundary that contrasts with the state's duration.
The later attribution branch repeats the focus act and specifies the signs as the object of sustained denial.

structural_cues: 22:55 uses a continuing construction followed by حَتَّىٰ, while the terminating event is marked as sudden.
22:57 resumes the exact focus denial root after the durative description.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies continuation, doubt, sudden termination, and renewed ك ذ ب; I infer that these are temporal phases of the focus's conditional denial. A live alternative is that the focus conditional names a discrete response and the later durative state concerns a broader class.

changed_reading.before: If they deny you describes a discrete adverse response.
changed_reading.after: If they deny you can inaugurate a durable regime of doubt and repeated denial that may continue for a long interval before ending abruptly.

context_deltas.mechanism: The object of denial shifts from you in the focus to the signs in 22:57; by 22:72 refusal is recognizable on faces and structurally approaches assault. Personal rejection, textual rejection, visible affect, and coercive action become stages of one possible escalation rather than synonyms.

activation_trace.role: The attribution branch anchors the escalation in declaring the addressed messenger false.
The same branch applied to the signs shifts the rejection's stated object beyond the messenger's person.
The literal face and forward surface branch makes rejection publicly legible in bodily appearance.
The contrary-to-recognition branch turns the visible reaction into refusal to acknowledge what is recited.

structural_cues: 22:57 changes the grammatical object from the messenger in 22:42 to the signs.
The branchless س ط و occurrence at 22:72 word 13 is used only as a structural cue for movement from facial refusal toward attack.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the object shift, visible facial reaction, and an uncited branchless assault verb; I infer a possible escalation chain among them. A live alternative is that the passages describe separate audiences or independent responses rather than sequential stages.

changed_reading.before: They deny you is chiefly a verdict about the messenger's truthfulness.
changed_reading.after: They deny you can abbreviate an embodied social escalation: reject the messenger, refuse the signs, display nonrecognition, and move toward coercion.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates a zoological motion branch inside ordinary form-II denial. It remains anchored because B007 belongs to the repeated focus root, while قَبْلَهُمْ and 22:46's travel supply a visible backward-motion mechanism; downstream prose should present it only as an exploratory image, never as a replacement lexical gloss.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The repeated ك ذ ب root at words 2 and 4 is adjacent to the backward temporal pointer قَبْلَهُمْ.

activation_trace.role: The wild creature that runs, stops, and looks behind contributes the outlier's literal motion image and figures denial as interrupted flight.
Temporal priority gives the backward glance a definite object: the peoples who came earlier.
The going and movement branch supplies a contextual journey on which stopping to inspect what lies behind becomes coherent.

changed_reading.before: Denial is a stationary verbal refusal.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, denial is figured as evasive motion that must pause and look backward at the fate of those before, with the historical names arresting the present flight.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because a tribal proper name is allowed to resonate with both return and a non-dominant count target. It remains packet-valid because the focus inventory explicitly preserves both mapped roots and 22:47 uses the count root in a time statement; downstream prose must label this a latent punning resonance, not an etymology or a claim about the tribe's name.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: عَادٌ at word 8 is a proper name under a split ع و د inventory that includes return and ع د د counting branches.

activation_trace.role: The proper-name branch preserves 'Ad as the literal referent and contains all further resonance.
The return-after-departure branch makes 'Ad a latent marker of the denial pattern's recurrence.
The non-dominant time-counter branch adds the exploratory possibility that recurrence is measured as well as repeated.
The explicit contextual counting of time activates the same mapped branch and gives the focus wordplay a local trigger.

changed_reading.before: 'Ad is only the second historical name in the sequence.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, 'Ad is a punning hinge where a returning historical pattern also enters a counted timescale, so recurrence is neither random nor temporally immediate.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the focus root's deceptive-garment branch to read denial as a social surface. It remains anchored through focus B009, the contextual false-speech branch, and the later facial surface; downstream prose should qualify it as a material analogy for public presentation, not as the ordinary sense of يُكَذِّبُوكَ.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus ك ذ ب inventory includes a garment that lies by its condition, while the verse predicates denial of a collective audience.

activation_trace.role: The deceptive-garment branch supplies a literal surface whose condition communicates falsely and figures denial as public presentation.
The uttered-speech branch keeps the material analogy tied to an actual communicative act.
The falsehood-and-batıl branch supplies the deceptive content worn by the collective public surface.
The face-as-forward-surface branch makes the group's later refusal visibly embodied and activates the garment analogy.

changed_reading.before: Denial consists in saying that the messenger is false.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, collective denial is also something publicly worn: speech, demeanor, and visible surface compose a presentation that lies by the condition it displays.

strongest_changes: The adjacent ق و م recurrence changes denial from a private opinion into a possible act of collective order-maintenance.
The repeated respite-then-seizure sequences change historical precedent from an immediate threat into a delayed, counted process.
The ruined settlement and travel sequence changes the people-list from remembered names into an index of materially readable traces.
The paired before-them and before-you constructions preserve coexisting lineages of denying communities and sent messengers.
Later duration and embodiment cues allow denial to coexist as a persistent state and as an escalation from attribution to visible and coercive refusal.
summary.what_was_special: The focus's dense repetition and its split inventory for 'Ad supported unusually strong latent activation: institutional, temporal, spatial, embodied, recursive, and material readings could coexist without replacing the plain denial narrative. Branch-distant motion, counting, and garment images remained live only with explicit containment.
remaining_uncertainties: The institutional transfer from أَقَامُوا in 22:41 to قَوْمُ in 22:42 may be lexical activation rather than a deliberate governance contrast.
The ruins in 22:45 may broaden the argument to unnamed towns rather than materialize the listed peoples one for one.
The paired قَبْل constructions may be ordinary chronology rather than an intentional two-line design.
The return-and-count resonance in 'Ad is packet-supported wordplay but remains too form-distant for an unqualified reading.
